thread:
liam: Heads up - saw a sharp egress jump on last month's bill, looks like ~1.1TB/day extra between us-west1 <-> eu-west1 for object storage. Not CPU / GPU related.

maya: Who's owning artifact replication? I remember we enabled async replication for model-artifacts-prod a few months back.

samir: That bucket had a change in lifecycle rules last week to keep artifacts for 90d. But replication shouldn't cause inter-region egress if it's the cloud provider-managed replication... hmm.

finance-ops: billing-alert: Alerting that cross-region egress exceeded threshold for project: inference-core. Estimated extra cost: ~$7.2k/month if continued.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 - Investigate unexpected storage egress (assigned: samir).

liam: I pulled a quick query from the billing export -> BigQuery. Pattern shows spikes coinciding with nightly model rollouts at 03:10 UTC. Logs show large PUT/GET traffic to gs://redwood-models-prod/* and a custom replication lambda fired right after releases.

samir: Sharing the query/snippet I used:
```
SELECT service.description, sku.description, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(usage_amount) as bytes
FROM `billing.project_line_items`
WHERE SKU.description LIKE "%Network egress%"
  AND usage_start_time >= "2026-02-01"
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY bytes DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

maya: That lambda was added to copy artifacts to eu for latency / warm caches. It uses `gsutil -m cp -r` currently (ugh). If it's doing full copies every rollout that's easily dumping TBs across regions.

liam: Exactly. I found the lambda invocation in Cloud Functions logs: 
```
functionName: replicateArtifacts
payload: { "version": "v2026-02-26-rc", "targets": ["eu-west1"] }
cmd: gsutil -m cp -r gs://redwood-models-prod/v2026-02-26-rc gs://redwood-models-eu/
```

ops-lead: That `-m cp -r` will re-copy entire trees. We should switch to object-level sync or rely on provider's cross-region replication. Do we need this lambda at all?

samir: The lambda was put in because we couldn't enable provider-managed replication due to customer tenancy isolation. But we can do `gsutil rsync -r -d` or use object checksums to avoid full copy. Better: enable conditional copy only for new objects.

finance-ops: If we can avoid the full copies that should reduce egress ~90% based on bytes observed. Can we estimate cost delta?

liam: Quick back-of-envelope: current extra egress ~33TB/month. At avg egress price $0.10/GB that's ~$3.3k/month; billing export shows added fees and inter-zone multipliers bringing total to the ~$7k estimate finance-ops mentioned. If we switch to delta replication, expect <4TB/month -> ~$400/month.

m aya: (typo) -> maya: Planning steps: 1) disable lambda for next nightly release (test env first), 2) enable `rsync`/checksum-based tool in staged rollout, 3) audit lifecycle + replication config, 4) add monitoring alert for bytes transferred between regions.

samir: I can change the function to use `gsutil rsync -c` and add `-n` dry-run flag for staging. Example: `gsutil -m rsync -r -c -d gs://redwood-models-prod/v2026-02-26-rc gs://redwood-models-eu/v2026-02-26-rc` That uses checksums to avoid full re-copies.

ops-lead: Also add object-level metadata to mark stable releases (e.g., x-redwood-release: v2026-02-26-rc) so replication can filter only release objects.

oncall-bot: runbook note: If egress spikes > $1k/day, paging policy will escalate to ops-lead and finance-ops.

finance-ops: Please tag any changes with cost-impact estimates in the PR. We'll hold a quick cost review before merging.

liam: Quick check on billing mapping: moving replication from lambda to `rsync` should also reduce PUT/GET request counts (request costs small but adds up at scale). Also check CDN / cache TTL - we might be re-pulling artifacts from origin to nodes cross-region.

samir: I dug into Cloud Audit logs. The largest transfers were objects >1GB (model shards). The lambda was parallelizing with -m and creating 64 concurrent transfers, which explains the throughput. Switching to rsync will still be parallel but skip identical objects.

maya: Action items and owners:
- samir: implement rsync-based replication in staging and run dry-run (ETA: today EOD)
- liam: create BigQuery dashboard with bytes-by-bucket and cross-region flows (ETA: tomorrow)
- ops-lead: disable lambda in prod for next release if staging looks good (ETA: after samir test)
- finance-ops: prepare cost-reduction estimate for next exec update (ETA: 2 days)

ops-lead: Also filing a follow-up to explore provider-side replication or dedicated inter-region transfer package (cheaper egress tiers). Ticket: INFRA-789.

billing-bot: Billing export row(s) attached for Feb 24-28: see link: https://console.cloud/billing/export/entries?range=2026-02-24_2026-02-28

liam: One more: add alert in Console to break down egress by callable source (cloud function vs provider replication vs CDN). Right now billing export groups it only by destination which is confusing.

samir: Running dry-run now, output: 
```
DRY RUN: would copy 2 objects, skip 84 objects (checksums match), total transfer would be 3.2GB
```

maya: Nice. That looks promising. Please paste the dry-run output into the PR.

finance-ops: Great work. If the numbers hold, this will move into next month's forecast and free up budget for extra dedicated GPU nodes if needed.

ops-lead: Closing loop: once staging validated we'll also add a guardrail: the replication function will refuse >5TB/day transfer and will require manual approval.

liam: Thanks everyone, keep me posted. I'll update the incident with the mitigation steps and expected cost delta.

samir: Updated INC-2026-042 with dry-run and will open PR shortly.

maya: :thumbsup:
